title: Async Commands, Background Work & Cancellation
objectives: Write async commands that never block
Avoid task leaks and UI polling
body:
# Async Commands, Background Work & Cancellation

## Async commands run on Tokio

```rust
#[tauri::command]
async fn run_rust_code(
    registry: State<'_, ExecutionRegistry>,
    sandbox: State<'_, SandboxPaths>,
    code: String,
) -> AppResult<RunResult> {
    execution::run_rust_code(&registry, &sandbox.root, &code).await
}
```

Long operations become awaitable without freezing either world. CPU-heavy or
blocking pieces go through `spawn_blocking`.

## Cancellation as a first-class feature

```rust
let handle = registry.register(execution_id);   // Arc<CancelHandle>
loop {
    if handle.is_cancelled() { kill(child).await; break; }
    match child.try_wait()? { Some(status) => break, None => sleep(100ms).await }
}
```

The frontend's Stop button hits `cancel_execution(executionId)` which flips the
flag; the poller kills within ~100 ms and reports partial output. Every spawned
task registers here — **no orphan runs**. That registry pattern lives in
`src-tauri/src/execution/registry.rs`.

## Bounded, structured, observable

- Cap concurrent background jobs (semaphore / fixed pool).
- Tie task lifetime to request/window scope; select! on shutdown signals.
- Report completion once, via the awaited response — not by polling stores.

## Smell: fire-and-forget spawns

`tokio::spawn(async { … })` whose handle you drop = unkillable, unobservable
work. If nothing awaits it, something must own its JoinHandle and cancellation
signal.

exercise.prompt: Implement `sum_until_limit(items:&[u64], cap:u64) -> u64` adding squares but stopping once running total would exceed cap (cooperative cancellation); print case 10/[1,2,3]→5 and 100/[4,9,1]→98.
